key_insight: CAPE extends acoustic perturbation equations to cavitating multiphase flows by embedding vapor mass transfer, mixture compressibility, and pressure-rate effects so cavitation noise sources can be resolved directly in the flow field.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical hydroacoustic tool for predicting and localizing cavitation-induced noise in marine and hydraulic systems, including cylinders and hydrofoils.
method: Formulate cavitation-consistent acoustic perturbation equations with phase-change and compressibility terms.
Use numerical verification on 1D wave-propagation tests with mesh/time-step refinement and a perfectly matched layer.
Apply the framework to cavitating flow past a circular cylinder and a NACA hydrofoil to identify tonal source mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Verification shows grid/time-step convergence, PML boundary-reflection suppression, and attenuation trends consistent with Stokes' sound attenuation law.
watch_item: The framework relies on accurate cavitation and phase-change modeling, so source predictions may be sensitive to constitutive choices and numerical treatment of localized collapse events.
paper_title: Cavitation Acoustic Perturbation Equations: A Computational Framework for Source-Resolved Multiphase Hydroacoustics
